13.t: Two women invite the simple: Wisdom offers a feast that leads to life; Folly offers stolen pleasures that lead to death.

14.t: Two women invite the simple: Wisdom offers a feast that leads to life; Folly offers stolen pleasures that lead to death.

15.t: Two women invite the simple: Wisdom offers a feast that leads to life; Folly offers stolen pleasures that lead to death.

16.t: Two women invite the simple: Wisdom offers a feast that leads to life; Folly offers stolen pleasures that lead to death.

17.t: Two women invite the simple: Wisdom offers a feast that leads to life; Folly offers stolen pleasures that lead to death.

18.t: Two women invite the simple: Wisdom offers a feast that leads to life; Folly offers stolen pleasures that lead to death.

1:14.t: "Cast lots with us": the KJV's "Cast in thy lot among us".

2:16.t: "The adulterous woman ... the wayward woman": the KJV's "the strange woman ... the stranger", a woman outside the covenant of marriage.

2:18.t: "The spirits of the dead": Hebrew rephaim; see Job 26:5.

3:15.t: "Rubies": the Hebrew peninim may be red coral or pearls.

3:34.t: James 4:6 and 1 Peter 5:5 quote this verse from the Greek: "God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble."

4:7.t: "Though it cost all you have": the KJV's "with all thy getting".

5:5.t: "The grave": the KJV's "hell"; Hebrew Sheol. 9:18 "The realm of the dead" is also Sheol.

7:27.t: "The grave": the KJV's "hell"; Hebrew Sheol. 9:18 "The realm of the dead" is also Sheol.

5:6.t: The KJV reads "Lest thou shouldest ponder the path of life". The Hebrew can be read either way.

5:15.t: "Cistern ... well ... fountain": images for a man's own wife, the proper and private source of sexual delight.

6:1.t: "Put up security": the KJV's "be surety", guaranteeing another person's debt.

6:26.t: "A prostitute can be had for a loaf of bread": the KJV's "a man is brought to a piece of bread". The Hebrew allows both.

7:14.t: "Fellowship offering": the KJV's "peace offerings". Meat from the offering had to be eaten within two days (Leviticus 7:16), so she has a feast ready.

7:22.t: "Bound for punishment in shackles": the Hebrew is difficult.

8:22.t: "Possessed": the KJV's word. The Hebrew qanah can mean "acquire", "possess", or "create"; the Greek reads "created".

Wisdom at creation: wisdom speaks as a person present with God before the world was made. The New Testament draws on this language for Christ, through whom all things were made and who is "the wisdom of God" (John 1:1-3, 1 Corinthians 1:24, Colossians 1:15-17).

10:1.t: Chapters 10-22:16 are the main collection of Solomon's proverbs, mostly two-line sayings in which the second line contrasts with or completes the first.

10:17.t: "Shows the way to life": the KJV's "is in the way of life". The Hebrew allows both.

10:19.t: "Sin is not ended by multiplying words": the KJV's "In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin", meaning that much talk leads to sin.

11:1.t: "Dishonest scales": the KJV's "a false balance". See Leviticus 19:35-36.

11:16.t: "Ruthless men gain only wealth": the KJV's "strong men retain riches".

11:30.t: "The one who is wise saves lives": the KJV's "he that winneth souls is wise", literally "he who takes lives (souls) is wise". It refers to winning people over by wise living.

11:31.t: 1 Peter 4:18 quotes this verse from the Greek.

12:26.t: The Hebrew of the first line is uncertain; the KJV reads "The righteous is more excellent than his neighbour".

13:8.t: "Cannot respond to threatening rebukes": the KJV's "the poor heareth not rebuke", that is, the poor are not worth threatening.

13:23.t: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult.

13:24.t: "The rod": correction given in love, not harshness. Compare Hebrews 12:5-11 and Ephesians 6:4.

14:4.t: "The manger is empty": the KJV's "the crib is clean". Without oxen there is no mess, but no harvest either.

14:9.t: "Making amends for sin": the Hebrew asham is the guilt offering (Leviticus 5).

14:32.t: "Seek refuge in God": the KJV's "hath hope in his death". The Greek and Syriac read "in his integrity".

15:11.t: "Death and Destruction": the KJV's "Hell and destruction", Hebrew Sheol and Abaddon. 15:24 "The grave" is also Sheol.

15:17.t: "Vegetables": the KJV's "herbs". "A fattened calf": the KJV's "a stalled ox".

15:25.t: "Boundary stones": the KJV's "border". Moving boundary markers was a common way of robbing the weak (Deuteronomy 19:14).

16:11.t: "The weights in the bag": merchants carried stone weights in a bag for weighing silver and goods.

16:15.t: "A rain cloud in spring": the KJV's "the latter rain", the spring rains that ripened the crops before harvest.

17:8.t: "A bribe": the KJV's "A gift". The verse observes how bribery works, without approving it (see 17:23).

17:19.t: "Builds a high gate": a picture of pride and showy display.

18:1.t: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult; the KJV reads "Through desire a man, having separated himself, seeketh and intermeddleth with all wisdom".

18:16.t: "A gift": here the word means a present, not a bribe.

18:24.t: "One who has unreliable friends soon comes to ruin": the KJV reads "A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly". The Hebrew is uncertain.
"A friend who sticks closer" (Hebrew davaq): the same verb as in Genesis 2:24, where a man is "united" to his wife; close, loyal attachment.

19:13.t: "Constant dripping of a leaky roof": see 27:15.

19:18.t: "Do not be a willing party to their death": the KJV's "let not thy soul spare for his crying". The Hebrew allows both.

19:22.t: The Hebrew of the first line is uncertain; the KJV reads "The desire of a man is his kindness".

20:1.t: "Beer": the KJV's "strong drink", fermented drink from grain or fruit.

20:10.t: "Differing weights": dishonest merchants kept one set of weights for buying and another for selling. See Deuteronomy 25:13-16.

20:23.t: "Differing weights": dishonest merchants kept one set of weights for buying and another for selling. See Deuteronomy 25:13-16.

20:16.t: "An outsider": the KJV's "a strange woman"; the Hebrew can be read either way.

20:26.t: "The threshing wheel": the wheel of a threshing cart, used to separate grain from chaff.

21:4.t: "The unplowed field": the KJV's "the plowing", Hebrew nir; many read "the lamp" instead.

21:9.t: "A corner of the roof": flat roofs were used as living space. See also 25:24.

21:12.t: "The Righteous One": the KJV reads "The righteous man ... but God overthroweth".

22:4.t: "Humility is the fear of the LORD": the KJV's "By humility and the fear of the LORD".

22:17.t: A new collection, "the sayings of the wise", begins here and runs to 24:22. It resembles the Egyptian Instruction of Amenemope.

22:20.t: "Thirty sayings": the KJV's "excellent things". The Hebrew shilshom (or shalishim) is uncertain; many read "thirty".

23:7.t: The KJV's "For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he" is the source of a well-known saying; in context it describes a stingy host.

23:14.t: "From death": the KJV's "from hell"; Hebrew Sheol.

23:34.t: "The rigging": the KJV's "the top of a mast".

24:23.t: A short collection, "These also are sayings of the wise", runs to 24:34.

25:1.t: Hezekiah was king of Judah about 715-686 BC; his scribes collected these proverbs (chapters 25-29).

25:7.t: "What you have seen with your eyes do not bring hastily to court": the KJV divides the verses differently: "the prince whom thine eyes have seen. Go not forth hastily to strive".

25:11.t: "A ruling rightly given": the KJV's "A word fitly spoken".

25:20.t: "On a wound": the KJV's "upon nitre", that is soda. The Greek reads "on a wound".

25:23.t: "Brings unexpected rain": the KJV reads "The north wind driveth away rain". In Israel the north wind usually brings dry weather.

25:27.t: "Search out matters that are too deep": the KJV reads "for men to search their own glory is not glory". The Hebrew is obscure.

26:4.t: The two sayings stand side by side on purpose: wisdom knows when to answer a fool and when not to.

26:10.t: The Hebrew of this verse is very obscure; the KJV reads "The great God that formed all things both rewardeth the fool, and rewardeth transgressors".

26:23.t: "Coating of silver dross": a glaze that makes a cheap clay pot look like silver.

27:9.t: The Hebrew of the second line is uncertain.

27:16.t: "Grasping oil with the hand": the KJV's "the ointment of his right hand, which bewrayeth itself".

27:20.t: "Death and Destruction": the KJV's "Hell and destruction", Hebrew Sheol and Abaddon.

29:18.t: "Revelation": the KJV's "vision", Hebrew chazon, prophetic revelation from God. "Cast off restraint": the KJV's "perish"; the Hebrew para means to run wild (Exodus 32:25).

30:1.t: Agur, Jakeh, Ithiel and Ucal are otherwise unknown. Some read the last words as "I am weary, God, I am weary and worn out".

30:8.t: "My daily bread": the KJV's "food convenient for me", literally "the bread of my portion". Compare Matthew 6:11.

30:28.t: "A lizard": the KJV's "The spider". The Hebrew semamit is probably the gecko.

30:31.t: "A strutting rooster": the KJV's "A greyhound"; the Hebrew is uncertain.

31:1.t: Lemuel is otherwise unknown; the name means "belonging to God".

31:10.t: This poem is an acrostic in Hebrew, each verse beginning with the next letter of the alphabet.

"A wife of noble character" (Hebrew eshet chayil): chayil means strength, ability or worth, used also of warriors ("mighty men of valor"). The KJV's "virtuous woman". Boaz calls Ruth an eshet chayil (Ruth 3:11).

1:7.t: "The fear of the LORD" (Hebrew yir'at YHWH): not terror but reverent awe that shapes the whole of life; the motto of Proverbs (9:10). "Beginning" (reshit) means both the starting point and the chief part. See Psalm 111:10.

"Wisdom" (Hebrew chokhmah): practical skill for living well before God, used also of craftsmen's skill (Exodus 28:3). "Fools" (evilim): not the mentally slow but the morally stubborn, who will not be taught.

1:20.t: "Wisdom calls aloud": wisdom is pictured as a woman calling in the streets (see chapters 8-9), in contrast to the adulterous woman of chapters 2, 5 and 7.

3:3.t: "Kindness and faithfulness" (Hebrew hesed ve'emet): when used of people, hesed is loyal kindness. See Genesis 24:27.

3:5.t: "Lean not on your own understanding ... acknowledge Him": "acknowledge" (da'ehu) means to know Him, in close relationship. "Make your paths straight" (yeyasher): make them level and direct.

4:23.t: "Guard your heart" (Hebrew lev): in Hebrew the heart is the center of thought, will and desire, not only the emotions. "Everything you do flows from it": the KJV's "out of it are the issues of life", the sources from which life springs.

8:30.t: "Constantly at His side": the Hebrew amon may mean "master craftsman" or "child, nursling" (the KJV's "one brought up with him").

9:1.t: Two women invite the simple: Wisdom offers a feast that leads to life; Folly offers stolen pleasures that lead to death.

9:10.t: "The Holy One" (Hebrew qedoshim): a plural of majesty, literally "holy ones", referring to God.

10:12.t: "Love covers over all wrongs" (Hebrew ahavah): love does not expose or dwell on the faults of others. Peter quotes this in 1 Peter 4:8, where the Greek word for love is agape, self-giving love. See also 1 Corinthians 13:7.

12:28.t: "Immortality" (Hebrew al-mavet): literally "no-death". The KJV reads "in the pathway thereof there is no death". A few Hebrew manuscripts and ancient versions read "to death".

14:31.t: "Shows contempt for their Maker": the poor bear God's image (Genesis 1:27), so to oppress them insults God Himself. Compare Matthew 25:40.

15:1.t: "A gentle answer" (Hebrew ma'aneh rakh): literally a "soft" answer, as the KJV has it.

15:33.t: "Humility comes before honor": see 18:12 and 22:4; Jesus taught the same (Luke 14:11).

16:3.t: "Commit" (Hebrew gol): literally "roll" your works onto the LORD, as one rolls a heavy burden onto another. See Psalm 37:5.

16:6.t: "Sin is atoned for" (Hebrew yekhuppar): the same verb as in the temple sacrifices (kipper, Leviticus 16). Here hesed and emet in a person's life show genuine repentance.

16:33.t: "The lot": stones or marked objects cast to reach a decision (Joshua 18:6, Acts 1:26). What looks like chance is under God's control.

17:17.t: "A friend loves at all times" (Hebrew ohev): constant love that does not depend on circumstances. "A brother is born for a time of adversity": the bonds of family show their worth in hard times.

18:10.t: "The name of the LORD": God's name stands for His character and presence (Exodus 34:5-7). To run to His name is to trust in who He is.

19:17.t: "Lends to the LORD": giving to the poor is treated as a loan to God Himself, who repays. Compare Matthew 25:40 and Luke 6:38.

20:27.t: "The human spirit is the lamp of the LORD" (Hebrew nishmat adam): the breath God gave (Genesis 2:7) is the conscience by which He searches a person's inmost being.

20:28.t: "Steadfast love and faithfulness", "kindness" (Hebrew hesed): in 20:28 the king's hesed mirrors God's own; in 21:21 a person's hesed is kindness.

21:21.t: "Steadfast love and faithfulness", "kindness" (Hebrew hesed): in 20:28 the king's hesed mirrors God's own; in 21:21 a person's hesed is kindness.

21:1.t: "The king's heart is a stream of water": a farmer channels irrigation water wherever he chooses; even the most powerful ruler is under God's control. The KJV reads "he turneth it whithersoever he will".

22:6.t: "Train a child in the way he should go" (Hebrew chanokh lanna'ar al-pi darko): "train" (chanakh) is also used of dedicating a house or temple (Deuteronomy 20:5). "In the way he should go" is literally "according to his way", which may mean the right way or the way suited to the child. It is a general principle, not a guarantee.

23:11.t: "Their Defender" (Hebrew go'alam): their kinsman-redeemer, the relative bound to protect the weak; here God Himself. See Exodus 6:6 and Ruth 4.

24:12.t: "He who weighs the heart": God sees past excuses. "Repay everyone according to what they have done" is echoed in Romans 2:6 and Revelation 22:12.

24:17.t: "Do not gloat when your enemy falls": see Matthew 5:44.

25:21.t: "Heap burning coals on his head": kindness to an enemy may bring burning shame and repentance. Paul quotes these verses in Romans 12:20.

27:6.t: "Wounds from a friend can be trusted" (Hebrew ne'emanim): "faithful" or "reliable", from aman, the root of "amen". Honest correction from a true friend is worth more than an enemy's flattery.

27:17.t: "As iron sharpens iron": literally "sharpens the face of his friend". Friends improve one another through honest exchange.

30:4.t: "What is His name, and what is the name of His son?": a riddle about the Creator, whom no human can grasp. Christians have read it as pointing to the Son who came down from heaven (John 3:13).

30:5.t: "Flawless" (Hebrew tseruphah): refined, like metal tested in fire. See Psalm 18:30.

31:26.t: "Faithful instruction" (Hebrew torat hesed): literally "the teaching of hesed", instruction marked by loyal kindness. The KJV's "the law of kindness".

31:30.t: "A woman who fears the LORD": the book ends where it began (1:7). The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom and the crown of a life well lived.
